records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) in as-cast (AC) state. Intervention: Isothermal aging at 600 °C for 20 hours. Processing: Specimens sealed in evacuated quartz tubes, furnace heated at 300 °C/h, held at target temperature for 3 h, aged for 20 h, then rapidly quenched in water. Test conditions: Tensile testing at room temperature with strain rate of 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. Structure change: Formation of high-density, small-sized (≈5.24 nm) L1₂ domains with perfectly ordered Ni₃Al structure (Ni/Al ≈ 3:1) and jagged phase boundaries (PBs). Property change: Fracture elongation deteriorated significantly (poorest ductility), UTS reduced, YS slightly increased compared to AC alloy. Mechanism: Enhanced chemical ordering increases APBE and shear modulus, promoting planar slip and strain localization; jagged PBs act as stress concentrators causing crack initiation. Evidence: measured. Quote: "As the aging temperature increases from ≈500 to 700 °C, fracture elongation deteriorates significantly, demonstrating a transition toward brittleness."

item.processing: Specimens sealed in evacuated quartz tubes, furnace heated at 300 °C/h, held at target temperature for 3 h, aged for 20 h, then rapidly quenched in water
item.test_conditions: Tensile testing at room temperature with strain rate of 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹
item.structure_change: L1₂ domains grew to ≈19.16 nm with off-stoichiometric composition (Ni/Al ≈ 2:1) and reduced order; formation of a Cr-rich particle (CRP)-free zone adjacent to phase boundaries
item.property_change: Fracture elongation rose dramatically (restoring ductility), UTS and YS recovered to levels comparable to AC alloy; optimal balance of ductility and strength
item.attributed_mechanism: Weaker ordering facilitates cross-slip and multiple slip systems; CRP-free zone enhances deformation compatibility and reduces stress concentration at PBs
quotes: At 750 °C, the UTS and YS recover to levels comparable to the AC alloy, and fracture elongation rises dramatically, thereby restoring ductility.

Property change: Fracture elongation rose dramatically (restoring ductility), UTS and YS recovered to levels comparable to AC alloy; optimal balance of ductility and strength. Mechanism: Weaker ordering facilitates cross-slip and multiple slip systems; CRP-free zone enhances deformation compatibility and reduces stress concentration at PBs. Evidence: measured. Quote: "At 750 °C, the UTS and YS recover to levels comparable to the AC alloy, and fracture elongation rises dramatically, thereby restoring ductility."

item.property_change: Fracture elongation deteriorated significantly (brittle transition), accompanied by a reduction in UTS and a slight increase in YS

Aging within the embrittlement‐prone regime enhances chemical ordering, increases the density of ordered domains, and induces jagged PBs, collectively triggering plastic instability and the ductile−to−brittle transition.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA in as-cast (AC) state. Intervention: Aging at 700 °C for 20 hours. Processing: Specimens sealed in evacuated quartz tubes, furnace heated at 300 °C/h, held at target temperature for 3 h, aged for 20 h, then rapidly quenched in water. Structure change: Continued evolution of L1₂ domains and phase boundaries within the embrittlement-prone regime (similar to 600A but with different ordering degree). Property change: Fracture elongation deteriorated significantly (brittle transition), accompanied by a reduction in UTS and a slight increase in YS. Mechanism: Aging within the embrittlement-prone regime enhances chemical ordering, increases the density of ordered domains, and induces jagged PBs, collectively triggering plastic instability. Evidence: measured. Quote: "As the aging temperature increases from ≈500 to 700 °C, fracture elongation deteriorates significantly, demonstrating a transition toward brittleness."

item.processing: Specimens sealed in evacuated quartz tubes, furnace heated at 300 °C/h, held at target temperature for 3 h, aged for 20 h, then rapidly quenched in water
item.test_conditions: Tensile testing at room temperature with strain rate of 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹
item.structure_change: Retention of duplex-phase microstructure with high thermal stability; some decline in fracture elongation but no catastrophic failure
item.property_change: UTS remains substantial at 837 MPa, YS holds at 355 MPa; fracture elongation declines but retains a notable 9.5%
item.attributed_mechanism: High thermal stability of the alloy system; aging outside the embrittlement regime suppresses excessive ordering and promotes ductile interphase transition zones
quotes: Even after aging at an extreme temperature of 1200 °C, the UTS remains substantial at 837 MPa, and the YS holds at 355 MPa.
Although fracture elongation declines at temperatures above 750 °C, the alloy aged at 1200 °C still retains a notable elongation of 9.5%.
In contrast, aging outside this regime suppresses excessive ordering and promotes the formation of ductile interphase transition zones, facilitating a brittle−to−ductile recovery.

item.intervention: Aging at 750 °C for 20 hours (specifically affecting CRPs near phase boundaries)
item.processing: Specimens sealed in evacuated quartz tubes, furnace heated at 300 °C/h, held at target temperature for 3 h, aged for 20 h, then rapidly quenched in water
item.structure_change: Dissolution of CRPs adjacent to PBs forming a CRP-free zone (≈few hundred nm) in the B2 edge region
item.property_change: Enhanced deformation compatibility, reduced stress concentration at PBs, and improved ductility compared to 600A
item.attributed_mechanism: CRPs are unstable at 750 °C and dissolve into the B2 matrix; the resulting CRP-free zone has lower hardness, allowing dislocations to transfer through PBs more easily
quotes: Thermodynamically, the CRPs are unstable at 750 °C, which tend to dissolve into the B2 matrix, increasing the Cr content in the B2 phase.
This dissolution process ceases once the Cr concentration in the B2 matrix reaches the equilibrium solubility at this temperature, thereby promoting and stabilizing the CRP‐free zone within B2.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA in as-cast (AC) state. Intervention: Aging at 600 °C for 20 hours (specifically affecting dislocation behavior). Processing: Specimens sealed in evacuated quartz tubes, furnace heated at 300 °C/h, held at target temperature for 3 h, aged for 20 h, then rapidly quenched in water. Test conditions: TEM and STEM analysis of deformed samples. Structure change: Formation of heavily localized planar slip bands along single {111} planes and long dislocation pairs with entangled morphology. Property change: Severe strain localization and reduced ductility due to hindered dislocation mobility and pile-ups at PBs. Mechanism: Strong LCO promotes planar dislocation slip through 'glide plane softening', leading to aggregation of dislocations and unsustainable working hardening. Evidence: measured. Quote: "Aging at 600 °C induces enhanced ordering with higher APBE, which intensifies this planarity, leading to pronounced strain localization and unsustainable working hardening."

item.intervention: Aging at 750 °C for 20 hours (specifically affecting B2 edge region)
item.processing: Specimens sealed in evacuated quartz tubes, furnace heated at 300 °C/h, held at target temperature for 3 h, aged for 20 h, then rapidly quenched in water
item.test_conditions: Transmission Kikuchi Diffraction (TKD) and EBSD analysis
item.structure_change: Lower density of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) and lower kernel average misorientation (KAM) in the B2 edge area compared to inner area
item.property_change: Reduced stress concentration at PBs and intact PBs in tensile fracture cross-section, indicating superior ductility
item.attributed_mechanism: The CRP-free zone allows deformation dislocations to transfer through PBs more easily, enhancing deformation compatibility and reducing stress concentration
quotes: A lower density of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) in the B2 edge area is observed compared to that in the B2 inner area, which indicates enhanced uniform plastic deformation and superior compatibility near the PBs.
Additionally, a lower kernel average misorientation (KAM) in the B2 edge area than in the inner area suggests a reduced stress concentration at the PBs.

item.processing: Specimens sealed in evacuated quartz tubes, furnace heated at 300 °C/h, held at target temperature for 3 h, aged for 20 h, then rapidly quenched in water
item.structure_change: CRPs in 600A exhibit higher Cr content than in AC, contributing to B2 phase hardening
item.property_change: Diminished ability of B2 phase to accommodate imposed strain, exacerbating stress mismatch at PBs

quotes: However, the CRPs embedded in the B2 phase of 600A alloy exhibit a higher Cr content than those in the AC alloy.
The mismatch in slip systems and stress‐relaxation capacity between the phases causes local stresses to rise rapidly at the sharp tips of the jagged PB.
